title: The Republic
author: Plato
blurb: Socrates asks what justice is — and imagines a whole city to find out. Home of the cave, the ring of invisibility and the philosopher-king.

justice.m: Fairness; giving each what is right.
justice.e: Justice was served when the thief returned the bike.

philosophers.e: Philosophers argue about what makes life good.

den.e: The bear slept in its den.

cards.title: Might is right?
cards.text: A brash teacher, Thrasymachus, claims justice is just whatever benefits the strong. Socrates spends the whole book proving him wrong.
cards.quote: justice the interest of the stronger
cards.qMean: Some argue 'justice' is just what helps the powerful.
cards.qLife: When rules seem written to protect the rich.
cards.cap: Bust of Socrates, Capitoline Museums · public domain

cards.title: If no one could see you
cards.text: A shepherd finds a ring that makes him invisible — and uses it for crime. Would anyone stay good if they could never be caught?
cards.quote: every one will do evil if he can.
cards.qMean: Some say everyone would do wrong if they couldn't be caught.
cards.qLife: Would you return extra change if no one would ever know?
cards.cap: A shepherd's rural scene · public domain

cards.title: Beginnings matter most
cards.text: Childhood shapes character more than anything later, so what children hear and see must be chosen with care.
cards.quote: the beginning is the most important part of any work
cards.qMean: The start of anything matters most.
cards.qLife: Good habits learned young last a lifetime.
cards.cap: Douris, red-figure school cup, c. 480 BC · public domain

cards.title: Wise rulers
cards.text: Plato's boldest claim: cities will have no rest from trouble until philosophers rule or rulers become philosophers.
cards.qMean: Leaders should be truly wise people.
cards.qLife: Wishing your city's mayor were an expert, not a celebrity.
cards.cap: David - The Death of Socrates · public domain

cards.title: The cave
cards.text: Prisoners chained in a cave see only shadows on a wall and think that is reality. One escapes into sunlight — and when he returns, no one believes him.
cards.quote: human beings living in an underground den which is open towards the light
cards.qMean: Most people mistake shadows for reality.
cards.qLife: Believing social-media highlights are what people's lives are really like.
cards.cap: Jan Saenredam, Plato's Cave, 1604 · public domain
